title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: recounting demurrage days for a rate or free-time dispute
content:
## Scope

When a demurrage invoice line of a per-container record under the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category is disputed on the rate-misapplied or free-time-misapplied ground, the desk recomputes it. This rule fixes the day count of that recomputation: clocks, chargeable days and slab positions.

## Rule

1. On a demurrage line disputed on the rate-misapplied or free-time-misapplied ground, the desk recomputes the line from the record's recorded dates and the product on the record.
2. Separate clock model: the demurrage clock of an import record runs from discharge to full gate-out against the import demurrage free days, and that of an export record from full gate-in to loading against the export demurrage free days. The days used are the stop date minus the start date in calendar days, the chargeable days are those beyond the free days, and the slab count starts at the first chargeable day.
3. Combined clock model: the merged clock runs from discharge to empty return on import and from empty pickup to loading on export, against the merged free days. On import the days up to and including the full gate-out date, and on export the days after the full gate-in date, are demurrage days. On export the slab count continues after the chargeable days of the detention line booked on the record.
4. Slab of each day by its position in the count: slab 1 up to the slab 1 length; slab 2 up to the first two lengths together; slab 3 up to all three lengths together; slab 4 beyond that.

## Recount checklist

| Step | Separate model | Combined model |
|---|---|---|
| Clock | the demurrage clock of the direction | the merged clock of the direction |
| Days counted as demurrage | every chargeable day of that clock | chargeable merged-clock days inside the terminal |
| Where the slab count starts | first chargeable day | import: first chargeable day; export: after the booked detention line's chargeable days |

## Worked example (hypothetical, an illustrative 15 merged free days and slab lengths of 4, 4 and 8, offset of one day)

A combined export record: empty pickup 1 June, full gate-in 20 June, loading 25 June, and a booked detention line of 4 chargeable days. The merged clock used 24 days; the gate-in date sits at position 19, so the demurrage days are positions 20 to 24, that is 5 days. Their slab count continues after the 4 detention days, so they take slab positions 5 to 9: four slab 2 days and one slab 3 day.
